prompts.text: Continue your conversation in whispers.
Speak as though you’re commentating on a very slow sporting event.
Let your voices gradually get slower. See how slow the conversation can become.
Lie beside each other and talk to the ceiling.
Sit or stand side by side. Choose something in the room to look at together.
Find an arrangement in which one of you is higher than the other. Swap after a while.
Take your shoes off while you talk.
Find a position in which neither of you is facing the other. Continue your conversation there.
Walk together at the pace of whoever is moving more slowly.
Keep talking while you slowly orbit each other.
Let one person’s small movements travel into the other person’s body. Swap who begins.
If you both want to, let your backs touch while you talk.
Find a comfortable distance. Change it together during the conversation.
Keep a light object between you using one finger each.
Balance an empty plastic bottle between your bodies. Decide together where it goes.
Both hold the same object while you talk. Let it move between you.
Each hold one end of a string. Keep it just slack enough to touch the floor while you talk.
Use the string to send each other signals while you talk. Invent what they mean.
Hold opposite ends of a rope or strip of fabric while you talk. Explore the distance and slack between you.
Each hold an edge of a piece of fabric. Find a shape you can keep changing together.
Make a small roof with the fabric. Have your conversation underneath it.
Draw on the same piece of paper while you talk. Neither of you owns a part of it.
Invent a mark for ‘I’m not sure’. Either of you can use it during the conversation.
Invent a gesture that means ‘stay with that thought’.
Choose a rule for how you’ll talk together. Try it, then change it.
Find a way to say ‘I disagree, but keep going’ without words. Then continue your conversation.
Take a little time to make a shared sound. Then start talking again.
Arrange three objects to show how you are together right now. You don’t have to agree on what the arrangement means. Then continue your conversation.
Each pair teaches the other a gesture or signal they invented.
Make a shape with a piece of fabric that needs all four of you.
Start a small movement and let it travel around the group. Keep talking as it travels.
Choose an object to stand for something none of you has said yet. Give it a place in the group.
